records.source: Καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος τοὺς δώδεκα μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς ἐξουσίαν πνευμάτων ἀκαθάρτων ὥστε ἐκβάλλειν αὐτὰ καὶ θεραπεύειν πᾶσαν νόσον καὶ πᾶσαν μαλακίαν.
records.gloss: And having summoned the twelve disciples of him he gave to them authority over spirits unclean so as to cast out them and to heal every disease and every sickness.
pieces: Jesus called {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} twelve disciples to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and gave them authority over unclean spirits, to drive them out, and to heal every disease and every illness.

L.1: And summoning {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} twelve disciples, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave them authority over unclean spirits, so as to cast them out and to heal every disease and every sickness.

R.1: Jesus called {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} twelve followers together. He gave them power over evil spirits so that they could make the spirits leave people. He also gave them power to heal every kind of sickness and disease.

decisions.choice: authority over unclean spirits: the right and power to command them
decisions.reason: The genitive names what the authority is over. The next words say what it is for: to cast the spirits out.

decisions.choice: every disease and every sickness: the same words as 4:23 and 9:35
decisions.reason: Matthew describes the twelve's work in the words he used for Jesus's own work. They share in what he does.

decisions.choice: unclean spirits: demons
decisions.reason: Unclean spirits are the demons of 10:8. They are unclean because they are opposed to God and defile those they control.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: A new section begins here, so Balanced and Readable name Jesus.

decisions.choice: evil spirits
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plainer phrase for the same beings.

records.heading: Jesus names twelve apostles

records.source: τῶν δὲ δώδεκα ἀποστόλων τὰ ὀνόματά ἐστιν ταῦτα· πρῶτος Σίμων ὁ λεγόμενος Πέτρος καὶ Ἀνδρέας ὁ ἀδελφὸς αὐτοῦ, Ἰάκωβος ὁ τοῦ Ζεβεδαίου καὶ Ἰωάννης ὁ ἀδελφὸς αὐτοῦ, Φίλιππος καὶ Βαρθολομαῖος, Θωμᾶς καὶ Μαθθαῖος ὁ τελώνης, Ἰάκωβος ὁ τοῦ Ἁλφαίου καὶ Θαδδαῖος, Σίμων ὁ Καναναῖος καὶ Ἰούδας ὁ Ἰσκαριώτης ὁ καὶ παραδοὺς αὐτόν.
records.gloss: Of the and twelve apostles the names are these: first Simon the [one] called Peter and Andrew the brother of him, James the [son] of Zebedee and John the brother of him, \v 3 Philip and Bartholomew, Thomas and Matthew the tax collector, James the [son] of Alphaeus and Thaddaeus, \v 4 Simon the Cananaean and Judas the Iscariot the [one] also having betrayed him.
pieces: The twelve apostles were these. First came Simon, known as Peter, with his brother Andrew; then James son of Zebedee, with his brother John;
Philip and Bartholomew; Thomas, and Matthew the tax collector; James son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus;
Simon the Cananaean, and Judas Iscariot, the man who betrayed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.2: Now the names of the twelve apostles are these: first, Simon, the [one] called Peter, and Andrew his brother; James the [son] of Zebedee, and John his brother;
L.3: Philip and Bartholomew; Thomas and Matthew the tax collector; James the [son] of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus;
L.4: Simon the Cananaean, and Judas Iscariot, the [one] who also betrayed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.2: Here are the names of the twelve apostles. First was Simon, who was also called Peter. Then there was his brother Andrew. There were James and his brother John, the sons of Zebedee.
R.3: There were Philip, Bartholomew, Thomas, and Matthew the tax collector. There were James the son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus.
R.4: And there were Simon the Zealot and Judas Iscariot. Judas was the one who later betrayed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: apostles: those sent out with authority to act for the one who sends them
decisions.reason: This is the only place Matthew uses the word. It comes from the verb "send out" used in 10:5 and 10:16.

decisions.choice: first: Peter heads the list
alternatives: the first one called, with no further sense
decisions.reason: Peter is named first in every list of the twelve (Mark 3:16; Luke 6:14; Acts 1:13), and he often speaks for them (16:16; 19:27).

decisions.choice: the Cananaean: from an Aramaic word meaning zealot, one zealous for God
decisions.reason: Luke 6:15 and Acts 1:13 call him "the Zealot". Whether this marks him as one who had fought against Roman rule or as one zealous for the law is not clear.

decisions.choice: Thaddaeus, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: Lebbaeus, or Lebbaeus called Thaddaeus, the reading of some manuscripts
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts read "Lebbaeus" here, and many later ones combine the two names. Luke 6:16 and Acts 1:13 name "Judas son of James" in this place in the list. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: betrayed: handed over to his enemies
decisions.reason: The verb means to hand over. Matthew uses it for Judas giving Jesus up (26:15-16) and for the disciples' own arrest (10:17, 19, 21). The meaning of "Iscariot" is not certain; it may mean "man from Kerioth".

decisions.choice: Simon the Zealot (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the name as Matthew gives it; Readable gives its meaning, as Luke does.

records.source: Τούτους τοὺς δώδεκα ἀπέστειλεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς παραγγείλας αὐτοῖς λέγων· Εἰς ὁδὸν ἐθνῶν μὴ ἀπέλθητε καὶ εἰς πόλιν Σαμαριτῶν μὴ εἰσέλθητε·
records.gloss: These the twelve sent out the Jesus having instructed them saying, Into a road of Gentiles not go off, and into a town of Samaritans not enter;
pieces: Jesus sent these twelve out, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} charged them: "Stay off the roads that lead to the Gentiles, and do not go into any Samaritan town.

L.5: These twelve Jesus sent out, instructing them, saying, "Do not go off onto [the] road of [the] Gentiles, and do not enter a town of [the] Samaritans;

R.5: Jesus sent out these twelve men. First {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told them what to do: "Do not go to people who are not Jews. And do not go into any town where Samaritans live.

decisions.choice: the road of the Gentiles: a road leading into Gentile country
decisions.reason: The words speak of a journey's direction. The twelve are not to take their mission beyond Israel.

decisions.choice: Samaritans: the people of Samaria, between Judea and Galilee
decisions.reason: The Samaritans worshiped the God of Israel but had their own temple and form of the law, and Jews and Samaritans were bitterly divided (John 4:9).

decisions.choice: a limit for this mission, not for all time
alternatives: a rule that the gospel is only for Israel
decisions.reason: Jesus comes first to Israel (15:24). After his resurrection he sends his disciples to all nations (28:19).

decisions.choice: people who are not Jews
decisions.reason: Readable says who the Gentiles are, as in 4:15.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and closes at the end of 10:42
alternatives: closing and reopening the quotation at each sentence
decisions.reason: Verses 5-42 are one speech, so the quotation marks stay open to the end.

records.heading: The twelve sent to the lost sheep of Israel

records.source: πορεύεσθε δὲ μᾶλλον πρὸς τὰ πρόβατα τὰ ἀπολωλότα οἴκου Ἰσραήλ.
records.gloss: go but rather to the sheep the being lost of house of Israel.
pieces: Go instead to the lost sheep, the people of Israel.

L.6: but go rather to the lost sheep of [the] house of Israel.

R.6: Go to the people of Israel. They are like sheep that are lost.

decisions.choice: the lost sheep, the house of Israel: the whole people is the lost flock
alternatives: only the lost ones within Israel
decisions.reason: As in 9:36, Jesus sees Israel as sheep without a shepherd. The same words come again in 15:24.

decisions.choice: lost sheep: Jeremiah 50:6; Ezekiel 34:4, 16
decisions.reason: The prophets call Israel lost sheep led astray by their shepherds, and God promises to seek the lost.

decisions.choice: the people of Israel
decisions.reason: "House" means the whole family or nation.

records.source: πορευόμενοι δὲ κηρύσσετε λέγοντες ὅτι Ἤγγικεν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν.
records.gloss: Going and proclaim saying that, Has come near the kingdom of the heavens.
pieces: Wherever you go, preach this: 'The kingdom of heaven has come near.'

L.7: And as you go, proclaim, saying, 'The kingdom of the heavens has come near.'

R.7: As you travel, tell people, 'The kingdom of heaven is coming near.'

decisions.choice: the same message as John's and Jesus's (3:2; 4:17)
decisions.reason: The twelve announce what Jesus announced. See 3:2 on "the kingdom of heaven".

decisions.choice: the same wording as 4:17 at each level
decisions.reason: The repeated message is given in the same words.

records.source: ἀσθενοῦντας θεραπεύετε, νεκροὺς ἐγείρετε, λεπροὺς καθαρίζετε, δαιμόνια ἐκβάλλετε· δωρεὰν ἐλάβετε, δωρεὰν δότε.
records.gloss: Ailing heal, dead raise, lepers cleanse, demons cast out; freely you received, freely give.
pieces: Heal those who are sick, raise the dead, make lepers clean, drive out demons. You received without paying, so give without charging.

L.8: Heal [the] sick, raise [the] dead, cleanse lepers, cast out demons. Freely you received; freely give.

R.8: Heal sick people. Bring dead people back to life. Heal people who have skin diseases. Make demons leave people. You did not pay for what you were given, so do not ask people to pay you.

decisions.choice: cleanse lepers: heal skin diseases that made a person unclean
alternatives: leprosy in the modern medical sense only
decisions.reason: As in 8:2-3, the word covered several skin diseases. Healing also made the person clean, able to return to worship and community.

decisions.choice: freely: as a gift, without payment
decisions.reason: The twelve received their power from Jesus at no cost, so they must not sell it. Compare Acts 8:18-20.

decisions.choice: raise the dead, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: the words are missing in many later manuscripts, and their place varies in others
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts lack "raise the dead", and others place it differently in the list. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: people who have skin diseases
decisions.reason: Readable describes the condition, as in 8:2.

records.source: μὴ κτήσησθε χρυσὸν μηδὲ ἄργυρον μηδὲ χαλκὸν εἰς τὰς ζώνας ὑμῶν, μὴ πήραν εἰς ὁδὸν μηδὲ δύο χιτῶνας μηδὲ ὑποδήματα μηδὲ ῥάβδον· ἄξιος γὰρ ὁ ἐργάτης τῆς τροφῆς αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: Not acquire gold nor silver nor copper in the belts of you, \v 10 not a bag for road nor two tunics nor sandals nor a staff; worthy for the worker of the food of him.
pieces: Do not provide yourselves with money for your belts, whether gold, silver, or copper.
Take no bag for the road, no second tunic, no sandals, and no staff. Workers have earned their food.

L.9: Do not acquire gold or silver or copper for your belts,
L.10: nor a bag for [the] road, nor two tunics, nor sandals, nor a staff; for the worker [is] worthy of {{gender:their|his}} food.

R.9: Do not take any money with you, not gold or silver or even copper coins.
R.10: Do not take a bag for the trip, or extra clothes, or sandals, or a walking stick. People who work should be given food. The people you serve will take care of you.

decisions.choice: acquire: get or provide for yourselves for the journey
decisions.reason: The verb means to get or procure. With 10:8 it may also forbid making money from the mission, but the list that follows is about what to take.

decisions.choice: gold, silver, copper in your belts: money of any kind
decisions.reason: Coins were carried in a fold of the belt. Copper coins were the smallest change, so the list rules out money altogether.

decisions.choice: a bag, a second tunic, a staff: the gear of a traveler
decisions.reason: A traveler carried a bag for food, a spare tunic for the cold, and a staff for walking and defense. Mark 6:8-9 allows a staff and sandals; Matthew and Luke 9:3 have Jesus forbid them. Each Gospel stresses that the twelve are to travel light and depend on God.

decisions.choice: the worker is worthy of his food: those they serve should feed them
alternatives: they must earn food by other work
decisions.reason: This is the reason for going without supplies. Luke 10:7 has "wages", and Paul cites the saying (1 Corinthians 9:14; 1 Timothy 5:18).

decisions.choice: The people you serve will take care of you.
decisions.reason: Readable states how the saying applies to the twelve.

records.source: εἰς ἣν δ’ ἂν πόλιν ἢ κώμην εἰσέλθητε, ἐξετάσατε τίς ἐν αὐτῇ ἄξιός ἐστιν· κἀκεῖ μείνατε ἕως ἂν ἐξέλθητε.
records.gloss: Into whatever now town or village you enter, inquire who in it worthy is; and there remain until you go out.
pieces: When you go into a town or village, ask who in it is worthy, and stay with that person until you move on.

L.11: And into whatever town or village you enter, inquire who in it is worthy, and stay there until you go out.

R.11: When you come to a town or village, find someone there who is ready to welcome you. Stay in that person's home until you leave that place.

decisions.choice: worthy: open to the message and ready to receive the messengers
decisions.reason: The worthy house is the one that receives them and their words (10:13-14).

decisions.choice: stay there: do not move from house to house
decisions.reason: They are to lodge in one home for their whole stay in that place.

decisions.choice: someone ... who is ready to welcome you
decisions.reason: Readable says what "worthy" means here.

records.source: εἰσερχόμενοι δὲ εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν ἀσπάσασθε αὐτήν·
records.gloss: Entering now into the house greet it;
pieces: As you go into the home, greet the family.

L.12: And as you enter the house, greet it;

R.12: When you go into a home, say, 'Peace be with you.'

decisions.choice: the house: the household, the people who live there
decisions.reason: A greeting is given to people, as 10:13 shows.

decisions.choice: greet it, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: some manuscripts add "saying, Peace to this house"
decisions.reason: A few manuscripts add the words of the greeting, as in Luke 10:5. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: say, 'Peace be with you'
decisions.reason: The usual greeting was a wish for peace, as 10:13 implies. Readable gives it.

records.source: καὶ ἐὰν μὲν ᾖ ἡ οἰκία ἀξία, ἐλθάτω ἡ εἰρήνη ὑμῶν ἐπ’ αὐτήν· ἐὰν δὲ μὴ ᾖ ἀξία, ἡ εἰρήνη ὑμῶν πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐπιστραφήτω.
records.gloss: And if indeed be the house worthy, let come the peace of you upon it; if but not it be worthy, the peace of you to you let return.
pieces: If that household is worthy, let your peace come to rest on it. But if it is unworthy, let the peace you gave come back to you.

L.13: And if the house is worthy, let your peace come upon it; but if it is not worthy, let your peace return to you.

R.13: If the people in that home welcome you, your blessing of peace will stay with them. If they do not welcome you, your blessing will come back to you.

decisions.choice: your peace: the greeting of peace, a blessing of God's wholeness and well-being
decisions.reason: The greeting "peace" was a prayer for God's good on the household. Spoken by Jesus's messengers, it is more than a custom.

decisions.choice: let your peace return to you: the blessing does not rest on those who refuse it
alternatives: the disciples must take back their words
decisions.reason: A blessing is pictured as going out and, if not received, coming back to the one who gave it.

decisions.choice: welcome you
decisions.reason: Readable says what being worthy means, as in 10:11.

records.source: καὶ ὃς ἂν μὴ δέξηται ὑμᾶς μηδὲ ἀκούσῃ τοὺς λόγους ὑμῶν, ἐξερχόμενοι ἔξω τῆς οἰκίας ἢ τῆς πόλεως ἐκείνης ἐκτινάξατε τὸν κονιορτὸν τῶν ποδῶν ὑμῶν.
records.gloss: And whoever not receives you nor hears the words of you, going out outside of the house or of the town that shake off the dust of the feet of you.
pieces: Some will not receive you or listen to your message. When you leave that house or that town, shake the dust from your feet.

L.14: And whoever does not receive you nor listen to your words, as you go out of that house or town, shake off the dust of your feet.

R.14: Some people will not welcome you or listen to you. When you leave their house or town, shake the dust off your feet. This will be a warning to them.

decisions.choice: shake off the dust: a sign that you are done with that place and it must answer for itself
decisions.reason: Paul and Barnabas do this in Acts 13:51. It shows that the messengers have done their part and leave the refusal to God's judgment (10:15).

decisions.choice: whoever does not receive you: a person or a whole town
decisions.reason: The next words speak of a house or a town, so a whole place may refuse.

decisions.choice: This will be a warning to them.
decisions.reason: Readable states what the gesture meant.

records.source: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀνεκτότερον ἔσται γῇ Σοδόμων καὶ Γομόρρων ἐν ἡμέρᾳ κρίσεως ἢ τῇ πόλει ἐκείνῃ.
records.gloss: Truly I say to you, more tolerable it will be for land of Sodom and Gomorrah in day of judgment than for the town that.
pieces: Truly I tell you, on the day of judgment the land of Sodom and Gomorrah will fare better than that town.

L.15: Truly I tell you, it will be more bearable for [the] land of Sodom and Gomorrah on [the] day of judgment than for that town.

R.15: I tell you the truth, on the day God judges all people, Sodom and Gomorrah will be punished less than that town.

decisions.choice: Sodom and Gomorrah: the cities God destroyed for their wickedness (Genesis 19)
decisions.reason: They were the byword for sin and judgment (Isaiah 1:9; Jude 7). A town that turns away God's messengers is worse off than they.

decisions.choice: more bearable: judgment will be heavier for those who refused greater light
decisions.reason: The comparison implies degrees of judgment, as in 11:22-24.

decisions.choice: Truly I tell you (L, B); I tell you the truth (R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:18, the solemn opening is given in the same words at each level.

decisions.choice: will be punished less (R)
decisions.reason: Readable states the comparison plainly.

records.source: Ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ ἀποστέλλω ὑμᾶς ὡς πρόβατα ἐν μέσῳ λύκων· γίνεσθε οὖν φρόνιμοι ὡς οἱ ὄφεις καὶ ἀκέραιοι ὡς αἱ περιστεραί.
records.gloss: Behold, I send out you as sheep in midst of wolves; be therefore shrewd as the serpents and innocent as the doves.
pieces: Remember, I am the one sending you out, like sheep with wolves all around. So be shrewd like snakes, yet harmless like doves.

L.16: Look, I send you out as sheep in [the] midst of wolves; so be shrewd as the serpents and innocent as the doves.

R.16: Listen! When I send you out, you will be like sheep with wolves all around them. So be careful and clever, like snakes. But be pure and do no wrong, like doves.

decisions.choice: sheep among wolves: defenseless people among those who will attack them
decisions.reason: The wolves are the persecutors of 10:17-23. The picture stresses danger and dependence on the shepherd who sends them.

decisions.choice: shrewd: wise and alert to danger; innocent: pure, without guile or harm
decisions.reason: The first word is used of sensible people (7:24; 25:2). The second means unmixed, with no evil in it. They must see danger clearly but never do wrong.

decisions.choice: I send you: the pronoun is stressed
decisions.reason: Jesus stresses that he himself sends them. That is their comfort in danger.

decisions.choice: look (L); remember (B); listen (R) (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

records.heading: Sheep among wolves

records.source: προσέχετε δὲ ἀπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων· παραδώσουσιν γὰρ ὑμᾶς εἰς συνέδρια, καὶ ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς αὐτῶν μαστιγώσουσιν ὑμᾶς·
records.gloss: Beware but of the men; they will hand over for you to councils, and in the synagogues of them they will flog you;
pieces: Be on guard against people. They will hand you over to local councils and whip you in their synagogues.

L.17: But beware of {{gender:people|men}}; for they will hand you over to councils, and in their synagogues they will flog you;

R.17: Be careful, because people will arrest you and take you to their courts. They will beat you with whips in their meeting places.

decisions.choice: councils and synagogues: local Jewish courts and the discipline they gave
decisions.reason: Towns had local councils, and synagogues could punish by flogging, up to forty lashes (Deuteronomy 25:3). Paul received thirty-nine lashes five times (2 Corinthians 11:24).

decisions.choice: hand you over: the word used of Judas and of Jesus's arrest
decisions.reason: The disciples will go through what their master goes through (10:4; 17:22; 20:18-19).

decisions.choice: {{gender:people|men}}
decisions.reason: The word means people in general, so the inclusive form is the default.

decisions.choice: meeting places
decisions.reason: Readable describes the synagogue, as in 4:23.

records.source: καὶ ἐπὶ ἡγεμόνας δὲ καὶ βασιλεῖς ἀχθήσεσθε ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ εἰς μαρτύριον αὐτοῖς καὶ τοῖς ἔθνεσιν.
records.gloss: and before governors and also kings you will be brought on account of me for a testimony to them and to the Gentiles.
pieces: Because of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} they will take you to stand before governors and kings. There you will bear witness to them and to the Gentiles.

L.18: and you will be brought before governors and also kings for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sake, as a testimony to them and to the Gentiles.

R.18: Because you follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, you will have to stand in front of governors and kings. Then you will tell them, and people who are not Jews, about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: governors and kings: Roman governors such as Pilate, and rulers such as the Herods
decisions.reason: Pilate was governor of Judea (27:2). Acts tells of apostles before Herod Agrippa, Felix, Festus and Agrippa II (Acts 12; 24-26).

decisions.choice: a testimony to them and to the Gentiles: a witness given before them
decisions.reason: The words can mean a witness to them or against them. Their trials become a chance to speak about Jesus, which also leaves those who reject him without excuse.

decisions.choice: them: the rulers, and perhaps the Jewish courts of 10:17
decisions.reason: "Them" stands beside "the Gentiles", so it likely points back to the rulers and the councils.

decisions.choice: people who are not Jews
decisions.reason: Readable says who the Gentiles are, as in 4:15.

decisions.choice: tell them ... about me
decisions.reason: Readable says what the testimony is about.

records.source: ὅταν δὲ παραδῶσιν ὑμᾶς, μὴ μεριμνήσητε πῶς ἢ τί λαλήσητε· δοθήσεται γὰρ ὑμῖν ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ τί λαλήσητε·
records.gloss: When but they hand over you, not be anxious how or what you should speak; it will be given for to you in that the hour what you should speak;
pieces: But when you are handed over, do not be anxious over how to answer or what to say. In that hour you will be given the words to speak.

L.19: But when they hand you over, do not be anxious how or what you are to speak; for what you are to speak will be given to you in that hour;

R.19: When people arrest you, do not worry ahead of time about what to say. God will give you the right words when you need them.

decisions.choice: it will be given: by God
decisions.reason: The passive points to God, as 10:20 makes plain.

decisions.choice: be anxious: worry, as in 6:25-34
decisions.reason: The same verb is used in the Sermon on the Mount. Jesus forbids fearful worry, not thought.

decisions.choice: God will give you
alternatives: it will be given to you
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the giver.

records.source: οὐ γὰρ ὑμεῖς ἐστε οἱ λαλοῦντες ἀλλὰ τὸ πνεῦμα τοῦ πατρὸς ὑμῶν τὸ λαλοῦν ἐν ὑμῖν.
records.gloss: not for you are the speaking but the Spirit of the Father of you the speaking in you.
pieces: The speaker will not be you; it will be your Father's Spirit speaking in you.

L.20: for you are not the ones speaking, but the Spirit of your Father [is the one] speaking in you.

R.20: The words will not really come from you. Your Father's Spirit will speak through you.

decisions.choice: the Spirit of your Father: God's Holy Spirit
decisions.reason: This phrase is found only here. It ties the Spirit to the Father who cares for them (10:29-31).

decisions.choice: in you: within you and through you
decisions.reason: The Spirit speaks from within the disciple; the words come through the disciple's own mouth.

records.source: παραδώσει δὲ ἀδελφὸς ἀδελφὸν εἰς θάνατον καὶ πατὴρ τέκνον, καὶ ἐπαναστήσονται τέκνα ἐπὶ γονεῖς καὶ θανατώσουσιν αὐτούς.
records.gloss: Will hand over and brother brother to death and father child, and will rise up children against parents and will put to death them.
pieces: One brother will hand another over to be killed, and a father his own child. Children will turn on their parents and send them to their death.

L.21: And brother will hand over brother to death, and father child, and children will rise up against parents and put them to death.

R.21: Brothers will hand each other over to be killed. Fathers will do this to their children. Children will turn against their parents and have them killed.

decisions.choice: children against parents: Micah 7:6
decisions.reason: Micah describes a time when families turn on each other. Jesus quotes it more fully in 10:35-36.

decisions.choice: put them to death: cause them to be executed by handing them over
alternatives: kill them with their own hands
decisions.reason: The children bring about their parents' death by denouncing them.

decisions.choice: brother: a brother by birth
decisions.reason: The verse is about members of one family, so the words name actual relatives.

records.source: καὶ ἔσεσθε μισούμενοι ὑπὸ πάντων διὰ τὸ ὄνομά μου· ὁ δὲ ὑπομείνας εἰς τέλος οὗτος σωθήσεται.
records.gloss: And you will be being hated by all because of the name of me; the but having endured to end, this one will be saved.
pieces: Everyone will hate you because of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name. But whoever holds out to the end will be saved.

L.22: And you will be hated by all because of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name; but the one who endures to [the] end, this [one] will be saved.

R.22: Everyone will hate you because you belong to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. But anyone who stays faithful to the end will be saved.

decisions.choice: because of my name: because you belong to me
alternatives: because you use my name in prayer
decisions.reason: A name stands for the person. They are hated for being his.

decisions.choice: to the end: to the end of the trial, even if it brings death
alternatives: to the end of the age only
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean "to the very end" or "to the end of the age" (24:13-14). Either way, one must hold firm however long the trouble lasts.

decisions.choice: will be saved: rescued for life in God's kingdom
decisions.reason: Some will be put to death (10:21), so this is rescue beyond death, as in 10:39.

decisions.choice: stays faithful
decisions.reason: Readable says what enduring means here.

records.source: ὅταν δὲ διώκωσιν ὑμᾶς ἐν τῇ πόλει ταύτῃ, φεύγετε εἰς τὴν ἑτέραν· ἀμὴν γὰρ λέγω ὑμῖν, οὐ μὴ τελέσητε τὰς πόλεις τοῦ Ἰσραὴλ ἕως ἂν ἔλθῃ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου.
records.gloss: When but they persecute you in the town this, flee into the other; truly for I say to you, not not you will finish the towns of Israel until comes the Son of the Man.
pieces: If they hunt you down in one town, escape to the next. Truly I tell you, the Son of Man will come before you have completed your work in the towns of Israel.

L.23: But whenever they persecute you in this town, flee to the other; for truly I tell you, you will not finish the towns of Israel before the Son of Man comes.

R.23: When people in one town attack you, escape to another town. I tell you the truth, the Son of Man will come before you have finished going to all the towns of Israel.

decisions.choice: before the Son of Man comes: the meaning is debated
alternatives: his coming at the end of the age
his coming in judgment on Jerusalem in AD 70
his joining the twelve during this mission
decisions.reason: The words recall Daniel 7:13, where one like a son of man comes to God and receives the kingdom. Some take it of the end of the age, with the mission to Israel going on until then; others of Jesus's resurrection and authority (28:18) or of the judgment on Jerusalem (24:30, 34). The translation keeps the open wording.

decisions.choice: finish the towns of Israel: complete the mission to them, or run out of places to flee
decisions.reason: The verb means to bring to an end. In context it may mean they will not finish preaching in Israel, or not run out of towns to flee to.

decisions.choice: persecute: pursue and harass
decisions.reason: The verb means to chase or pursue, and so to persecute (5:10-12).

decisions.choice: Truly I tell you (L, B); I tell you the truth (R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:18, the solemn opening is given in the same words at each level.

records.source: Οὐκ ἔστιν μαθητὴς ὑπὲρ τὸν διδάσκαλον οὐδὲ δοῦλος ὑπὲρ τὸν κύριον αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: Not is a disciple above the teacher nor a slave above the master of him.
pieces: No disciple ranks above the teacher, and no servant above the master.

L.24: A disciple is not above the teacher, nor a slave above {{gender:their|his}} master.

R.24: Students are not more important than their teacher. Servants are not more important than their master.

decisions.choice: not above the teacher: followers will be treated as their master is
alternatives: a rule about respect for teachers
decisions.reason: The proverb explains why the disciples will be persecuted: Jesus has been, so they will be (10:25).

decisions.choice: slave: one owned by a master and bound to serve him
decisions.reason: The word is the one for a slave. Jesus and Paul use it of those who belong wholly to God (Philippians 1:1).

decisions.choice: {{gender:their|his}}
decisions.reason: The proverb applies to all disciples, so the inclusive form is the default.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m2) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: ἀρκετὸν τῷ μαθητῇ ἵνα γένηται ὡς ὁ διδάσκαλος αὐτοῦ, καὶ ὁ δοῦλος ὡς ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: Enough for the disciple that he become as the teacher of him, and the slave as the master of him.
pieces: It is enough for disciples to become like their teacher, and for servants to become like their master.

L.25: [It is] enough for the disciple to become like {{gender:their|his}} teacher, and the slave like {{gender:their|his}} master.

R.25: Students should be content to become like their teacher. Servants should be content to become like their master.

decisions.choice: enough: they should expect no better treatment than their master's
decisions.reason: To share the master's lot is both all they can expect and an honor.

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it, and Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: εἰ τὸν οἰκοδεσπότην Βεελζεβοὺλ ἐπεκάλεσαν, πόσῳ μᾶλλον τοὺς οἰκιακοὺς αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: If the master of the house Beelzebul they called, how much more the household of him.
pieces: If they have called the head of the house Beelzebul, how much more will they insult the members of his household!

L.25: If they called the master of the house Beelzebul, how much more those of his household!

R.25: People have called the head of the house Beelzebul, the ruler of demons. So they will be even quicker to insult the rest of his family.

decisions.choice: Beelzebul: a name for Satan, the ruler of the demons
decisions.reason: The name recalls Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron (2 Kings 1:2). In the Gospels it is a name for the prince of demons (12:24-27). It echoes the charge of 9:34.

decisions.choice: Beelzebul, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: Beelzebub, the reading of some Latin and Syriac witnesses
Beezebul, the spelling of a few Greek manuscripts
decisions.reason: The spelling "Beelzebub" follows 2 Kings 1:2 and is familiar from older translations, but the Greek manuscripts read "Beelzebul" or "Beezebul". Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the master of the house: Jesus himself
decisions.reason: Jesus is the one called Beelzebul (9:34; 12:24). Some suggest a play on words, as "zebul" may mean "dwelling", making Beelzebul "lord of the house".

decisions.choice: his household, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The master of the house is a figure in a picture, so the pronoun takes no span, though the picture points to Jesus.

decisions.choice: the ruler of demons
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the name and says who is meant.

records.source: Μὴ οὖν φοβηθῆτε αὐτούς· οὐδὲν γάρ ἐστιν κεκαλυμμένον ὃ οὐκ ἀποκαλυφθήσεται, καὶ κρυπτὸν ὃ οὐ γνωσθήσεται.
records.gloss: Not therefore you should fear them; nothing for is covered which not will be revealed, and hidden which not will be known.
pieces: So do not be afraid of them. Everything now covered will be uncovered, and every secret will come to light.

L.26: So do not fear them; for nothing is covered that will not be revealed, and [nothing] hidden that will not be known.

R.26: So do not be afraid of those people. Everything that is hidden now will be shown. Every secret will be made known.

decisions.choice: what is covered will be revealed: the message now spoken in private will be made public
decisions.reason: Verse 27 applies the saying to Jesus's teaching. Whatever their enemies do, the truth will come out. The same saying is used of exposing sin in Luke 12:2-3.

decisions.choice: do not fear them: the persecutors of 10:17-25
decisions.reason: "Them" refers to those who will hate and persecute the disciples. "Do not fear" comes three times (10:26, 28, 31).

records.heading: Fear God, not people

records.source: ὃ λέγω ὑμῖν ἐν τῇ σκοτίᾳ, εἴπατε ἐν τῷ φωτί· καὶ ὃ εἰς τὸ οὖς ἀκούετε, κηρύξατε ἐπὶ τῶν δωμάτων.
records.gloss: What I say to you in the darkness, say in the light; and what into the ear you hear, proclaim on the housetops.
pieces: The things I tell you in the dark, you must say in the open; the things you hear as a whisper, you must proclaim from the housetops.

L.27: What I tell you in the darkness, speak in the light; and what you hear in the ear, proclaim on the housetops.

R.27: I am telling you things now in private. Tell them openly to everyone. What you hear from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in a whisper, shout from the rooftops.

decisions.choice: in the dark, in the light: in private, in public
decisions.reason: Darkness and light stand for what is hidden and what is open. Jesus teaches the twelve privately; they must tell it to all.

decisions.choice: the housetops: flat roofs, a place to call out to the whole street
decisions.reason: Houses had flat roofs reached by stairs, and announcements could be made from them.

decisions.choice: as a whisper
decisions.reason: "In the ear" means spoken quietly to one person.

records.source: καὶ μὴ φοβεῖσθε ἀπὸ τῶν ἀποκτεννόντων τὸ σῶμα τὴν δὲ ψυχὴν μὴ δυναμένων ἀποκτεῖναι· φοβεῖσθε δὲ μᾶλλον τὸν δυνάμενον καὶ ψυχὴν καὶ σῶμα ἀπολέσαι ἐν γεέννῃ.
records.gloss: And not be afraid of the killing the body, the but soul not being able to kill; fear but rather the being able both soul and body to destroy in Gehenna.
pieces: Those who kill the body have no power to kill the soul, so do not be afraid of them. Be afraid instead of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} who can destroy soul and body alike in hell.

L.28: And do not be afraid of those who kill the body but are not able to kill the soul; but rather fear {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} who is able to destroy both soul and body in Gehenna.

R.28: Do not be afraid of people. They can kill your body, but they cannot kill your soul. The one you should fear is God. He can destroy both your body and your soul in hell.

decisions.choice: the one who is able to destroy: God
decisions.reason: Only God judges and destroys in Gehenna (Isaiah 66:24; James 4:12). The next verses speak of the same God as a caring Father, so fear of him goes with trust.

decisions.choice: soul: the person's life and self beyond bodily death
decisions.reason: Here the word means the part of a person that killing the body cannot reach.

decisions.choice: Gehenna: the place of final judgment
decisions.reason: As in 5:22, Gehenna was the valley of Hinnom by Jerusalem, whose name became a name for the fire of God's judgment.

decisions.choice: destroy: ruin in the final judgment
decisions.reason: The word means to ruin or destroy. Whether this means ending existence or lasting ruin is not settled by this verse (compare 25:46).

decisions.choice: Gehenna (L); hell (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:22, Literal keeps the place name.

decisions.choice: The one you should fear is God.
decisions.reason: Readable names God, following the meaning decision.

records.source: οὐχὶ δύο στρουθία ἀσσαρίου πωλεῖται;
records.gloss: Not two sparrows for an assarion are sold?
pieces: Two sparrows sell for {{units:a penny|an assarion}}, do they not?

L.29: Are not two sparrows sold for an assarion?

R.29: Two sparrows are sold for only {{units:a penny|an assarion}}.

decisions.choice: two sparrows for an assarion: almost worthless birds
decisions.reason: An assarion was a small Roman copper coin worth a sixteenth of a denarius, a laborer's daily wage. Sparrows were the cheapest birds sold for food.

decisions.choice: {{units:a penny|an assarion}}
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use a small modern coin by default, with the original coin as the alternative. Literal keeps the original coin.

decisions.choice: a statement instead of a question
alternatives: Are not two sparrows sold for a penny?
decisions.reason: The question expects "yes"; Readable gives the answer.

records.source: καὶ ἓν ἐξ αὐτῶν οὐ πεσεῖται ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν ἄνευ τοῦ πατρὸς ὑμῶν.
records.gloss: And one of them not will fall to the ground apart from the Father of you.
pieces: Yet not one of them falls to the ground apart from your Father.

L.29: And not one of them will fall to the ground apart from your Father.

R.29: But not even one of them falls to the ground and dies unless your Father allows it.

decisions.choice: apart from your Father: without his will and care
decisions.reason: The phrase is short. It means nothing happens to even a sparrow outside the Father's rule. Some manuscripts add "will" to make this plain.

decisions.choice: fall to the ground: die
decisions.reason: A bird falling to the ground is one that dies.

decisions.choice: and dies unless your Father allows it
decisions.reason: Readable spells out both phrases, following the meaning decisions.

records.source: ὑμῶν δὲ καὶ αἱ τρίχες τῆς κεφαλῆς πᾶσαι ἠριθμημέναι εἰσίν.
records.gloss: Of you and even the hairs of the head all numbered are.
pieces: As for you, even the hairs on your head have all been counted.

L.30: But even the hairs of your head are all numbered.

R.30: God even knows how many hairs are on your head.

decisions.choice: your hairs are numbered: God has counted them
decisions.reason: "Your" stands first for emphasis: if God cares for sparrows, how much more for you. The passive points to God.

decisions.choice: God even knows
decisions.reason: Readable names God and says what the counting shows.

records.source: μὴ οὖν φοβεῖσθε· πολλῶν στρουθίων διαφέρετε ὑμεῖς.
records.gloss: Not therefore fear; than many sparrows are worth more you.
pieces: So do not be afraid. You are worth more than a whole flock of sparrows.

L.31: So do not be afraid; you are worth more than many sparrows.

R.31: So do not be afraid. You are worth much more to God than many sparrows.

decisions.choice: worth more than many sparrows: from the lesser to the greater
decisions.reason: If God cares for birds sold for almost nothing, he cares far more for his children (6:26).

decisions.choice: to God
decisions.reason: Readable says whose valuing is meant.

records.source: Πᾶς οὖν ὅστις ὁμολογήσει ἐν ἐμοὶ ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ὁμολογήσω κἀγὼ ἐν αὐτῷ ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ πατρός μου τοῦ ἐν οὐρανοῖς·
records.gloss: Everyone therefore who will confess in me before the men, will confess also I in him before the Father of me the in heavens;
pieces: So everyone who openly confesses {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} before others, I also will confess before {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father in heaven.

L.32: Everyone therefore who will acknowledge {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} before {{gender:people|men}}, I also will acknowledge {{gender:them|him}} before {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father who [is] in [the] heavens;

R.32: Some people will say openly that they are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} followers. I will tell {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father in heaven that they belong to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: confess in me: openly declare that one belongs to me
decisions.reason: The phrase follows an Aramaic way of speaking. It means to stand openly on someone's side.

decisions.choice: before my Father: at the judgment
decisions.reason: Jesus pictures himself speaking for his followers when God judges (7:21-23; 25:31-34).

decisions.choice: {{gender:people|men}}; {{gender:them|him}}
decisions.reason: The words apply to everyone, so the inclusive forms are the default.

records.source: ὅστις δ’ ἂν ἀρνήσηταί με ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ἀρνήσομαι κἀγὼ αὐτὸν ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ πατρός μου τοῦ ἐν οὐρανοῖς.
records.gloss: whoever but denies me before the men, will deny also I him before the Father of me the in heavens.
pieces: But whoever denies {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in front of people will be denied by {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in the presence of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father in heaven.

L.33: but whoever denies {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} before {{gender:people|men}}, I also will deny {{gender:them|him}} before {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father who [is] in [the] heavens.

R.33: But some people will say in front of others that they do not know {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. I will tell {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father in heaven that I do not know them.

decisions.choice: deny me: refuse to own me, disown me
decisions.reason: Peter does this in 26:70-74. To deny Jesus is to say one has nothing to do with him.

decisions.choice: {{gender:people|men}}; {{gender:them|him}}
decisions.reason: As in 10:32.

decisions.choice: will be denied by me
decisions.reason: Balanced turns the second clause into the passive to keep the sentence plain.

records.source: Μὴ νομίσητε ὅτι ἦλθον βαλεῖν εἰρήνην ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν· οὐκ ἦλθον βαλεῖν εἰρήνην ἀλλὰ μάχαιραν.
records.gloss: Not think that I came to bring peace on the earth; not I came to bring peace but a sword.
pieces: Do not imagine that {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} coming was to bring peace on earth. I came to bring a sword, not peace.

L.34: Do not think that I came to bring peace on the earth; I did not come to bring peace, but a sword.

R.34: Do not think I came to bring peace to everyone on earth. I did not come to bring peace. I came to bring a sword that divides people.

decisions.choice: a sword: division, not war
decisions.reason: Verses 35-36 explain the sword: it cuts families apart. Luke 12:51 has "division". Jesus's followers are not to fight with swords (26:52).

decisions.choice: not peace: the result of his coming, not its aim
alternatives: Jesus does not care about peace
decisions.reason: Jesus blesses peacemakers (5:9). But because people respond to him in different ways, his coming divides even families.

decisions.choice: bring: literally "throw" or "cast"
decisions.reason: The verb suggests something cast onto the earth with force.

decisions.choice: a sword that divides people
decisions.reason: Readable says what the sword stands for.

records.heading: A sword that divides households

records.source: ἦλθον γὰρ διχάσαι ἄνθρωπον κατὰ τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ καὶ θυγατέρα κατὰ τῆς μητρὸς αὐτῆς καὶ νύμφην κατὰ τῆς πενθερᾶς αὐτῆς, καὶ ἐχθροὶ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου οἱ οἰκιακοὶ αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: I came for to set at variance a man against the father of him and a daughter against the mother of her and a daughter-in-law against the mother-in-law of her, \v 36 and enemies of the man the household of him.
pieces: My coming will set son against father, daughter against mother, and daughter-in-law against mother-in-law.
People's enemies will be those of their own household.

L.35: For I came to set a man against his father, and a daughter against her mother, and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law;
L.36: and the enemies of the {{gender:person|man}} [will be] the members of {{gender:their|his}} household.

R.35: I came to turn sons against their fathers and daughters against their mothers. I came to turn daughters-in-law against their mothers-in-law.
R.36: A person's enemies will be people in their own family.

decisions.choice: Micah 7:6
decisions.reason: Jesus takes up Micah's words about a time when families turn on each other. In Micah the son dishonors his father; here the division comes because some follow Jesus and others do not.

decisions.choice: a man against his father: a son
decisions.reason: The pairs are family members, and Micah 7:6 has "son".

decisions.choice: the man's enemies: anyone's
alternatives: the man of the first line only
decisions.reason: The last line is a general saying, as in Micah, and applies to women and men alike.

decisions.choice: son
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say which family member is meant. Specific relatives take no gender span.

decisions.choice: {{gender:person|man}}; {{gender:their|his}}
decisions.reason: The last line is general, so the inclusive form is the default.

records.source: ὁ φιλῶν πατέρα ἢ μητέρα ὑπὲρ ἐμὲ οὐκ ἔστιν μου ἄξιος· καὶ ὁ φιλῶν υἱὸν ἢ θυγατέρα ὑπὲρ ἐμὲ οὐκ ἔστιν μου ἄξιος·
records.gloss: The loving father or mother above me not is of me worthy; and the loving son or daughter above me not is of me worthy;
pieces: Whoever puts love for father or mother above {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is not worthy of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and whoever puts love for son or daughter above {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is not worthy of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

L.37: The one who loves father or mother more than {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is not worthy of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; and the one who loves son or daughter more than {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is not worthy of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}};

R.37: People who love their father or mother more than they love {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} do not deserve to be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} followers. People who love their son or daughter more than they love {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} do not deserve to be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} followers.

decisions.choice: worthy of me: fit to belong to me as my disciple
decisions.reason: The word is used of what fits or deserves something. Jesus says who truly belongs to him; he is not grading people's merit.

decisions.choice: love more than me: put before me
decisions.reason: Jesus asks for first place, not for lack of love at home. Luke 14:26 says the same with the stronger idiom "hate". Jesus also upholds honor for parents (15:4).

decisions.choice: do not deserve to be my followers
decisions.reason: Readable says what being worthy of Jesus means.

records.source: καὶ ὃς οὐ λαμβάνει τὸν σταυρὸν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀκολουθεῖ ὀπίσω μου, οὐκ ἔστιν μου ἄξιος.
records.gloss: and who not takes the cross of him and follows after me, not is of me worthy.
pieces: Whoever refuses to pick up their own cross and walk behind {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is not worthy of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

L.38: and whoever does not take {{gender:their|his}} cross and follow after {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is not worthy of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

R.38: People who will not carry their cross and come after {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} do not deserve to be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} followers.

decisions.choice: take his cross: as a condemned man carried his cross to execution
decisions.reason: Under Rome a condemned man carried the crossbeam to the place of death (27:32). Following Jesus means being ready to suffer and die for him. This is the first mention of the cross in Matthew, before Jesus speaks plainly of his death (16:21, 24).

decisions.choice: worthy of me: fit to belong to me as my disciple
decisions.reason: The word is used of what fits or deserves something. Jesus says who truly belongs to him; he is not grading people's merit.

decisions.choice: follow after me (L); walk behind me (B)
decisions.reason: The words picture walking behind Jesus on the road to the cross.

records.source: ὁ εὑρὼν τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ἀπολέσει αὐτήν, καὶ ὁ ἀπολέσας τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ εὑρήσει αὐτήν.
records.gloss: The having found the life of him will lose it, and the having lost the life of him on account of me will find it.
pieces: Those who secure their own life will lose it, and those who lose their life for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sake will find it.

L.39: The one who has found {{gender:their|his}} life will lose it, and the one who has lost {{gender:their|his}} life for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sake will find it.

R.39: People who try to keep their life for themselves will lose it. But people who give up their life for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} will find it.

decisions.choice: life: one's life and self, here and in the age to come
decisions.reason: The same word is "soul" in 10:28. The saying plays on two senses: life in this world, and the true life God gives.

decisions.choice: has found: has secured or kept safe, as by denying Jesus
alternatives: has discovered the meaning of life
decisions.reason: In context, to "find" one's life is to save it by giving up following Jesus (10:33). Compare 16:25.

decisions.choice: secure (B); try to keep (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what finding means here; the second "find" keeps the word.

records.source: Ὁ δεχόμενος ὑμᾶς ἐμὲ δέχεται, καὶ ὁ ἐμὲ δεχόμενος δέχεται τὸν ἀποστείλαντά με.
records.gloss: The receiving you me receives, and the me receiving receives the having sent me.
pieces: To welcome you is to welcome {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and to welcome {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is to welcome {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

L.40: The one who receives you receives {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and the one who receives {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} receives the [one] who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

R.40: When people welcome you, they are welcoming {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. And when they welcome {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, they are welcoming God, who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: receiving you receives me: a messenger stands for the one who sent him
decisions.reason: As the Jewish saying held, one sent stands in the place of the sender. So the twelve stand for Jesus, and Jesus for God (John 13:20).

decisions.choice: the one who sent me: God the Father
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of himself as sent by God (15:24).

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Readable names God.

records.heading: Welcome and its reward

records.source: ὁ δεχόμενος προφήτην εἰς ὄνομα προφήτου μισθὸν προφήτου λήμψεται, καὶ ὁ δεχόμενος δίκαιον εἰς ὄνομα δικαίου μισθὸν δικαίου λήμψεται.
records.gloss: The receiving a prophet in name of a prophet reward of a prophet will receive, and the receiving a righteous in name of a righteous reward of a righteous will receive.
pieces: Anyone who receives a prophet because that person is a prophet will be given a prophet's reward; anyone who receives a righteous person because that person is righteous will be given the reward of the righteous.

L.41: The one who receives a prophet in [the] name of a prophet will receive a prophet's reward, and the one who receives a righteous [person] in [the] name of a righteous [person] will receive a righteous [person]'s reward.

R.41: Anyone who welcomes a prophet because that person speaks for God will get the same reward a prophet gets. And anyone who welcomes a righteous person because that person lives right before God will get the same reward a righteous person gets.

decisions.choice: in the name of a prophet: because he is a prophet
alternatives: by the authority of a prophet
decisions.reason: The phrase gives the reason for the welcome: the guest is received for what he is.

decisions.choice: a prophet's reward: the reward a prophet receives
alternatives: a reward given by a prophet
decisions.reason: Those who support God's messengers share in their reward. Compare the widow of Zarephath and Elijah (1 Kings 17:8-24).

decisions.choice: prophet, righteous person: those who speak for God and those who live faithfully, perhaps among Jesus's own messengers
decisions.reason: Matthew pairs prophets and the righteous (13:17; 23:29). Here they likely include Jesus's followers sent out as messengers.

decisions.choice: because that person speaks for God; because that person lives right before God
alternatives: in the name of a prophet; in the name of a righteous person
decisions.reason: Readable says what the titles mean.

records.source: καὶ ὃς ἂν ποτίσῃ ἕνα τῶν μικρῶν τούτων ποτήριον ψυχροῦ μόνον εἰς ὄνομα μαθητοῦ, ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, οὐ μὴ ἀπολέσῃ τὸν μισθὸν αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: And whoever gives to drink one of the little ones these a cup of cold only in name of a disciple, truly I say to you, not not he will lose the reward of him.
pieces: And whoever gives one of these little ones no more than a cup of cold water because that one is a disciple—truly I tell you, such a person will never lose their reward."

L.42: And whoever gives one of these little ones only a cup of cold [water] to drink in [the] name of a disciple, truly I tell you, {{gender:they|he}} will by no means lose {{gender:their|his}} reward."

R.42: These followers of {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}} may seem small and unimportant. But suppose someone gives one of them just a cup of cold water because that one is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} follower. I tell you the truth, that person will surely be rewarded."

decisions.choice: these little ones: Jesus's disciples, humble and of no account in the world
decisions.reason: Matthew uses "little ones" for believers in 18:6, 10, 14. The phrase "in the name of a disciple" shows that disciples are meant.

decisions.choice: a cup of cold water: the smallest kindness
decisions.reason: Cool water was a welcome gift in a hot land. Even the least help given to a disciple will be rewarded.

decisions.choice: will by no means lose his reward: God will surely reward him
decisions.reason: The double negative is strong. The speech that began at 10:5 ends here; 11:1 returns to the story.

decisions.choice: Truly I tell you (L, B); I tell you the truth (R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:18, the solemn opening is given in the same words at each level.

decisions.choice: These followers of mine may seem small and unimportant.
decisions.reason: Readable explains whom Jesus calls little ones.

decisions.choice: {{gender:they|he}}; {{gender:their|his}}
decisions.reason: The promise is for anyone who helps a disciple, so the inclusive form is the default.
